links.outcome: Reading level (FKGL, FRES) of LLM patient education responses about ACL surgery
links.effect: DeepSeek FKGL 8.9 vs ChatGPT 14.2 (p<0.001); FRES 61.3 vs 32.7 (p<0.001). ChatGPT text was at a college-level reading grade, DeepSeek nearer general audience.
links.quote: DeepSeek had lower FKGL (8.9 vs. 14.2, p < 0.001) and higher FRES (61.3 vs. 32.7, p < 0.001), indicating greater ease of reading for a general audience.

links.outcome: Clarity and readability of AI patient education outputs for laypersons
links.effect: DeepSeek clarity 3.9 vs ChatGPT 3.0 (p<0.001); DeepSeek FKGL 8.9 vs 14.2, so ChatGPT output less comprehensible to lay readers.
links.quote: DeepSeek's answers were clearer and more accessible to laypersons (mean clarity 3.9 vs. 3.0, p < 0.001)

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates two LLM tools (ChatGPT-4o DeepResearch vs. DeepSeek R1 DeepThink) on patient education FAQs using expert surgeon grading and readability formulas, but does not test a health system deployment practice or guardrail.
